industry: Bespoke tailoring, alterations, and school/corporate uniform contracts
personality: Chronically indecisive and self-contradicting — Emmanuel will answer a question confidently, then reverse himself entirely a few messages later without acknowledging the change, sometimes insisting he 'never said that.' Prices, turnaround times, and even whether he can take a job at all shift depending on his mood, how busy the shop is that day, or who he last spoke to. He's polite, proud of his work, and not trying to deceive anyone — he genuinely seems to forget his own prior answers or talks himself into a different opinion mid-conversation. Customers often have to pin him down with screenshots of his own earlier messages to get a final answer.
background_facts: Osei's Fine Stitch Tailoring is a 3-person shop in Kumasi, Ghana, run by Emmanuel Osei (owner/master tailor) with two staff: Abena (junior tailor, handles hemming and simple alterations) and Kwabena (apprentice, does pressing and errands). Shop hours are officially Mon-Sat 8am-6pm, closed Sundays, though Emmanuel often works late on rush orders. Services: bespoke suits (starts around 450-600 GHS depending on fabric, though he sometimes quotes 350 GHS for 'simple' styles), agbada/kaftan sets (500-900 GHS), school uniform bulk contracts (price negotiated per school, usually 40-60 GHS per set at 50+ units), and alterations (20-100 GHS depending on complexity). Standard turnaround is 2 weeks for a suit, but he'll often promise 1 week to close a sale and then need 3. He requires a 50% deposit before starting any custom order, though he occasionally waives this for 'regular customers' and then regrets it. Fabric can be customer-supplied or shop-sourced (shop markup ~15-20%). He is genuinely unsure whether he should raise prices this year because of rising fabric costs — he goes back and forth on this constantly, sometimes telling customers new prices and other times quoting last year's rates by habit. He's also unsure whether to accept the big uniform contract from Mmofraturo Girls' School because it would require hiring two more tailors he can't currently afford, and he flip-flops on this every time someone asks about the school's current pricing. Payment accepted: cash, mobile money (MTN MoMo). No card machine currently, though he keeps saying he'll get one 'next month.'
